sections.html:
Two offices divide the work. The Assessor decides what a parcel is worth for tax purposes. The Collector of Revenue sends the bills and takes the money, from Room 100 of the Courthouse Annex at 311 E High Street, Jefferson City 65101. Call the Collector at 573-634-9124 on weekdays between 8 in the morning and 4:30 in the afternoon. A 24 hour drop box is outside the Annex entrance facing High Street.

The County Clerk keeps the hearing calendar for the Board of Equalization, and the Missouri State Tax Commission supervises assessors and hears appeals after the local board rules. Send value questions to the Assessor and bill questions to the Collector. Tax money is shared among the state, several municipalities, rural fire districts, the public library and the school districts.

A real estate bill is payable once you have it and in any case by December 31. Mail is judged by postmark. Bills go out during November, and the Collector says to phone if yours has not arrived by the second week of December, because a bill you never got still carries the tax and late fees.

  • Charges in the first year of delinquency can climb as high as 25%.
  • Unpaid tax is a lien that follows the real estate, so a buyer takes on whatever is owed.
  • If your lender escrows the tax, hand the bill to the lender.
  • A seller who still gets a bill for a house already sold should give the Collector the buyer's name and address.

The online system takes cards with a 2.25% convenience fee and e-checks with a $1.75 fee, and an e-check needs 5 to 7 days to clear. You can also call 855-568-0066, walk in or mail a check. A December 31 postmark is on time, and the drop box is open until midnight that night. At the counter the office accepts cash, personal check, cashier's check, bank draft, money order or card, and one check may cover several bills.

sections.h2: How the amount is worked out
sections.html:
Start with assessed value, divide by 100, then multiply by the levy. Assessed value is a fraction of market value, and the fraction depends on how the parcel is classified.

Class of real estateShare of value assessed
Residential19%
Agricultural12%
Commercial32%

Voters and the taxing districts set the levies, and the Assessor's page links a rate sheet. The county's real estate tax page explains the method. Before you estimate a bill for a house you are selling, find out which taxing districts cover the parcel.

sections.h2: How to challenge a Cole County valuation
sections.html:
Begin with an informal conversation with the Assessor. It is voluntary and available on weekdays during office hours. Show proof of market value: photographs, an inspection report, a recent appraisal or sales nearby. The Assessor's role is to keep values in line with the current market.

The Board of Equalization conducts the formal review, and RSMo 137.275 puts the filing deadline on the second Monday in July. The board includes the County Commissioners, a non-voting Assessor and appointees, with two city appointees for parcels inside Jefferson City. The County Clerk records the proceedings and mails each taxpayer the written decision.

A dispute that remains can go to the State Tax Commission. RSMo 138.430 allows the appeal within the period stated in that chapter or 30 days after the local board finishes, whichever ends later. These sessions are typically held in September and October before one Administrative Hearing Officer. Expect to bring an appraisal, and a lawyer is optional.

A parcel that has been delinquent for three years can go into the county's certificate sale. It begins at 10 in the morning on the fourth Monday of August at the Cole County Courthouse, a date that RSMo 140.150 sets across Missouri. Paying the tax, penalty, interest and costs to the Collector before the sale stops it for that parcel.

  • The News Tribune in Jefferson City runs the parcel list for three consecutive weeks beforehand.
  • The winning bidder holds a certificate of purchase, and the owner has a year from the sale to redeem.
  • Liens on the property survive the sale and the redemption window.
  • A winning bidder who fails to pay risks a 25% penalty plus a prosecuting attorney fee.

An owner who is behind and thinking of selling can ask the Collector for a current payoff. No tax is paid to that office at the moment of a sale, so request any payoff figure in writing through your title company.

sections.h2: Who pays when a house changes hands
sections.html:
Whoever owns the house in the fall pays the November bill, and after a mid-year sale that is the buyer. Taxes are generally prorated, so the buyer receives a credit at closing for the days or months the seller held the property. The buyer then pays the entire bill by December 31.

The county sits in central Missouri below the Missouri River, with Jefferson City as the seat and state capital. Estimates for July 1, 2025 show 77,908 people and 33,956 housing units. About 67.9% of units are owner-occupied, the 2020 to 2024 median value is $229,600 and median household income is $74,876. Rent has a median of $834, and 154 building permits were issued in 2025.

Before you list, ask the Collector for your parcel's balance and confirm the taxing districts on your last statement. A title company can then show the tax line at closing, and the Collector needs only the new owner's mailing address afterward. Cash Home Buyers can buy a house with back taxes or a lien problem and let the closing agent clear the balance from the price.

faqs.q: What day does Cole County property tax become late?
faqs.a: After December 31. The bill is payable on receipt, mailed payments are judged by postmark and the courthouse drop box stays open until midnight that night. Charges during the first delinquent year can run up to 25%.

faqs.q: Can I count on the Collector mailing my bill?
faqs.a: Bills are mailed in November. If none has come by the second week of December, phone 573-634-9124. The obligation and late fees stand even when a bill is lost.

faqs.q: Until what date can I appeal to the Board of Equalization?
faqs.a: The second Monday in July, with the filing made through the County Clerk. An informal meeting with the Assessor can come earlier.

faqs.q: Do the buyer or the seller owe the tax after a mid-year sale?
faqs.a: The buyer owes the whole bill due in December. Proration between the parties normally gives the buyer a credit at closing, and nothing is paid to the Collector during closing. A seller who still gets the bill should send the Collector the buyer's address.

faqs.q: How many years of unpaid tax lead to a sale?
faqs.a: Three. After that the parcel can be offered at the August certificate sale, and the owner may still pay what is due before the sale or redeem within a year after it.
